text:
Loss choice plausibly limits SASRec ranking, but does not establish why Electronics is weak. [gSASRec’s 2024 summary](https://www.ijcai.org/proceedings/2024/0939.pdf) attributes poor performance partly to negative-sampling overconfidence; proposes gBCE with more negatives, recommending 128–256 negatives and calibration t=0.75. [Scaled cross-entropy research (2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.14238) supports testing full-softmax CE, or scaling the sampled denominator when full softmax is expensive. [Correcting the LogQ Correction (RecSys 2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.09331) addresses sampling bias: popular in-batch items receive disproportionate negative pressure, and correction must account for the positive being always included rather than sampled. Sampling correction and false-negative mitigation address different problems.

Hardest-negative selection risks penalizing plausible future positives. [R²NS (WWW 2026)](https://renzhaochun.github.io/assets/pdf/WWW_2026_Camera_Ready.pdf) uses uniform warm-up, efficient global candidate retrieval, then curriculum sampling uniformly within a gradually narrowed top-ranked set; reports that hard mining introduced too early can underperform uniform sampling. Practical experiment inference: hold architecture fixed and compare single-negative BCE, multi-negative BCE/gBCE, sampled CE, and corrected sampled CE under equal GPU-second limits; add warm-start stochastic hard mining only after establishing these baselines. Exclude padding, target collisions and observed training positives; remaining unseen items still have uncertain relevance. Do not use held-out interactions to identify false negatives. Select by pinned four-category macro validation HR@10, inspecting Electronics separately; training margins, calibration improvements and published gains do not establish gains under the 99-negative evaluator.
